body: Chief-architect disposition (2026-08-29): keep two estimands separate by type: (A) a task-conditioned perceptual-boundary track with a declared human instruction/grain, and (B) an evidence-backed resolved narrative hierarchy. Never promote B to gold for A; enforce circularity through the FeatureUseLedger. A public boundary API must not use a bare Int level: level needs both depth and declared grain/instruction semantics, with the exact vocabulary deferred to an ADR. Do not create a segment module or implementation beads yet; the first implementation step is an Int-level ADR plus a frozen, named, multi-story decision spike. Existing features + acquire + story contracts remain the home until a second consumer appears. Humans are offline benchmark evidence only, never a runtime requirement. Keep per-rater series and evaluate leave-story/family/provider-family-out with tolerance curves, Pk, WindowDiff, count bias, Brier/calibration, and a split-half human ceiling. Treat repeated LLM calls as clustered by provider/config, not as independent raters; preserve numerator plus eligible and attempted denominators, retain failed/missing calls in derivation receipts, forbid bare vote fractions, and require a named calibration model before calling any score a probability. StoryAtlas should render the perceptual-boundary track and resolved hierarchy as separate synchronized visual channels, not collapse one into the other. A separate observation notes that align dSens currently conflates no sensory evidence with 0.0; that repair is explicitly outside the visualization slice.
